title: Economy Mode: Conversation Slimming + Hybrid Fidelity (scratchpad)
body:
Purpose:
Quick brain dump for an "economy mode" product feature that proactively reduces token/compute cost for long-running conversational sessions by combining: aggressive context slimming, selective compression, and hybrid fidelity fallback (cheap-model summarizer + full-model finalization). This doc is notes + rough user stories + implementation pointers. Not polished.

Problem statement:
- Customers with long lived sessions (assistant/chatbots, tutoring, customer support) are hitting unpredictable token bills.
- Current fallbacks are blunt: swap to smaller model or truncate context bluntly which breaks UX.
- Need a graceful, configurable “economy” behavior that preserves critical context and degrades in predictable, explainable ways.

Hypothesis:
If we provide a per-session Economy Mode that performs selective slimming (drop/noise removal + anchor preservation) and an optional cheap summarizer step, then tail token cost can drop 30–60% while user-visible regressions are small and measurable.

High level flow (user opt-in or developer toggle):
1) Session enters Economy Mode after defined triggers: token budget exhausted, time idle, user toggled, or admin policy.
2) System computes slim map: mark message anchors (instructions, system message, recent 2 utterances, named entities).
3) For older messages: either compress (summarize) with small summarizer model (embedding+L2 or gpt-mini) OR prune non-anchors; attach short summary token.
4) Generate produce via normal model; allow two-phase option: cheap model generates a draft, full model finalizes if budget allows.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want a session-level "economy" flag that limits per-session token spend so we can cap cost for free-tier users.
- As an end-user, I want the assistant not to repeat irrelevant backstory when I ask a new question after long idle time.
- As an SRE, I want telemetry that shows per-session token delta before/after slimming and a fallback audit trail.

Accept criteria / metrics:
- Cost reduction: median per-session token count reduced by >=30% for sessions hitting the trigger.
- Quality: human eval A/B: final answer judged non-inferior (<=10% drop) on intent-carrying tasks.
- Latency: added slimming step should add <=200ms (summarizer warm/cold varies). Two-phase full finalization is asynchronous (optional) and must degrade gracefully.
- Observability: for any slimmed session, we can produce a human-readable compacted transcript and the slimming decisions.

Config knobs (developer facing):
- trigger: {token_threshold, idle_minutes, manual_toggle, plan_tier}
- strategy: {prune, summarize, hybrid}
- summarizer_model: model id
- anchor_rules: regex + heuristics (mentions, system messages, last N turns, entities)
- two_phase: {off, async_finalize, sync_finalize}
- cost_budget_per_session: integer tokens or currency

Runtime considerations (notes for infra/runtime team):
- Summarizer should be small/cheap and support streaming. Keep quantized variant in cache.
- Ideally run slimming in the same GPU node to avoid network overhead; fallback to CPU worker if necessary.
- KV cache: need to preserve exact token offsets when we rehydrate session for finalization. Make slim metadata lightweight (store anchors ids + summary text).
- Batching: slimming requests can be batched per summarizer to improve efficiency—watch latency SLO.

UX examples / prompts (devs can change):
- Summarizer prompt: "Condense these 10 messages into a 2-sentence factual summary preserving named entities and unresolved actions. Output JSON: {summary, anchors}"
- System message behavior: always preserve system-level instructions verbatim.

Rollout plan (safe incremental):
1) Internal dogfood: enable on 10% sessions for internal teams, collect A/B metrics.
2) Beta: opt-in developer flag on hosted API. UI/Console shows predicted savings and last-slim preview.
3) Opt-out opt-in for end users via SDK flags and console toggles.

Experiment ideas:
- Compression vs prune: randomize sessions to measure UX difference.
- Anchor aggressiveness: tune anchor N and entity threshold.
- Two-phase finalize: compare cost/latency tradeoffs; measure how often finalize changes output materially.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: summarizer may surface PII when condensing. Need redaction hooks pre-summarize or KMS/HSM for summarize artifacts.
- Auditability: customers want to see what was discarded—how long to retain slim metadata? retention policy required.
- Billing attribution: how to bill the summarize step and finalize step consistently (split across models?).
- Edge cases: critical instructions buried in old messages (we must ensure anchors detect them).

Data we need to measure impact:
- sample sessions with full transcripts + human labels for intent preservation (1000 sessions per workload).
- token distribution histograms pre/post
- per-session latency + summarizer cold starts

Implementation todo (short checklist):
- [ ] prototype summarizer prompt + small model selection (Mika)
- [ ] design slim metadata schema (Noah) -> lightweight list-of-anchors + summary text
- [ ] console UI mock for opt-in/budgets (Priya)
- [ ] telemetry: new events (economy.enter, economy.slim.apply, economy.finalize)
- [ ] security review: PII redaction before summarize

Notes to self / questions to discuss in sync on Wed:
- Should we expose a "slim-preview" API so apps can show users what got compressed before sending final request? Pros: transparency. Cons: extra round trips.
- How to integrate with existing QoS routing policies? e.g., for active canary we might prefer less aggressive slimming.

Rough API sketch (developer toggle):
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/messages
headers: X-Redwood-Economy: {on|off}
body: {message, economy_options: {strategy: "summarize", budget_tokens: 800, two_phase: "async_finalize"}}

This is a sandbox note — keep it rough. Will flesh into a proper PRD if the initial signals look promising.

-- cassandra
